findings.title: Gemma2 silently loses its sliding window under SDPA when attn_logit_softcapping is None
findings.claim: Delta commit d80d3f99 (#954) added `masking_module_patcher=apply_compact_sdpa_sliding_window_masking_patch` to the gemma2 family (models/gemma2.py:35). That patcher deliberately returns `None` instead of a dense mask when the compact conditions hold (runtime/masking.py:79-107 `_can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window`: sdpa, no padding mask, no cache, dropout-free-or-no-grad, seq_len > sliding_window), delegating the look-back limit to the family's SDPA replacement. For mistral/ministral that replacement is `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window`, which honours it via `_compact_sliding_window_sdpa`. For gemma2 it is `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2`, whose `softcap is None` branch falls through at attention.py:729-738 to plain `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward(...)` WITHOUT passing `sliding_window`; that function accepts `**kwargs` and never applies a window (attention.py:174-241 only does causal SDPA). Before the delta the gemma2 family had no masking patcher, so the mask was always dense and carried the window - the hole is new in this delta. This is an incomplete fix of the same defect class as OPQ-337 / Bazalt #811 ('sliding window dropped under SDPA when attention_mask is None') and directly contradicts Slate #397's invariant.
findings.failure_scenario: Reproduced end to end on transformers-installed Gemma2. `Gemma2Config(hidden_size=32, num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=8, sliding_window=4, attn_logit_softcapping=None, attention_dropout=0.0)`, `_attn_implementation='sdpa'`, float64, `input_ids` of shape (1, 24): unpatched logits vs logits after `apply_runtime_patches()` + `apply_model_patches(model)` differ by 0.4171 max-abs while mean |logit| is 0.0802 - a 5x-the-mean deviation. Control with `attn_logit_softcapping=50.0` (the config default) on the same weights and inputs: 6.1e-08. Direct unit check at the attention level (H=2, S=16, D=8, window 4, float64): `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window` matches an explicit windowed reference to 0.0, `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2(..., softcap=None, sliding_window=4)` deviates 1.9777 from that reference and matches plain full-causal SDPA to exactly 0.0. Disabling `attn_logit_softcapping` is the documented workaround for using SDPA/flash with Gemma2, so this is a realistic configuration; every sliding layer then trains and evaluates on full causal attention with no error or warning.
evidence: packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:729-738 - `return vmap_sdpa_attention_forward(module, query, key, value, attention_mask, dropout=dropout, scaling=scaling, **kwargs)` - `sliding_window` is a named parameter of the enclosing function (line 678) so it is NOT in **kwargs and is dropped entirely

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/components/attention.py:174-241 - `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward` has no sliding-window handling at all; it only computes `is_causal` and calls SDPA

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/runtime/masking.py:89-107 - `_can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window` returns True (mask becomes None) without consulting `attn_logit_softcapping`

packages/opaque-patches/src/opaque/api/patches/transformers/models/mistral.py:32-33 and ministral.py:32-33 pair the same patcher with `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window`, which does honour the window (attention.py:277-305)

git show 4b13d82:.../components/attention.py:160-196 - at the delta base the gemma2 softcap=None branch delegated to stock `sdpa_attention_forward` and gemma2 had no masking patcher, so the dense mask always carried the window
measured: patched-vs-upstream Gemma2ForCausalLM logits max|diff| = 0.4170584599232694 with attn_logit_softcapping=None vs 6.142407904530245e-08 with 50.0, same weights/inputs
findings.fix_sketch: In `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_gemma2`, route the `softcap is None` fall-through to `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward_sliding_window(..., sliding_window=sliding_window, ...)` instead of `vmap_sdpa_attention_forward`, so the compact windowed path is used whenever the mask is None. Alternatively make `_can_use_compact_sdpa_sliding_window` refuse the None-mask skip for gemma2 when softcapping is disabled. Add a parity test that instantiates a gemma2 with `attn_logit_softcapping=None`, `sliding_window < seq_len`, sdpa and no attention mask - the existing sliding-window parity variant always supplies a mask, so this branch is untested.

findings.title: New random-allocation lru_cache retains native PLD handles past calibrate's cache teardown, with a docstring that denies it
findings.claim: Slate #437 replaced every per-method `functools` PLD cache with a bounded registry whose native handles `calibrate` drops in its `finally` (calibration.py:210-212, 356-357 `_clear_all_native_caches()`). Delta commit 20dd47aa (#881) introduced a new `@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=8)` over `_native.random_allocation_gaussian_pld`. Its return type is `Pld`, which `_base.py:60` aliases as `_native.Pld` - a Rust-backed handle - so the module docstring's claim that the cache holds 'immutable Python Pld objects (no native handles), so it is self-limiting and needs no byte budget or destructor' is false, as is the '~0.5 MB per entry at the default config' sizing comment. The cache is not registered in `_native_cache._registry`, so `_clear_all_native_caches()` is a no-op for it and only the module-private `clear_random_allocation_caches()` (called from tests only) empties it.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured on the current tree with the freshly built extension. (a) `cal.calibrate(cal.epsilon_budget(3.0, delta=1e-5), lambda nm: k_out_of_t(gaussian(nm), k=4, t=64, allocation='block'), 0.5, 4.0)` leaves `epoch_pld.cache_info() == CacheInfo(hits=0, misses=14, maxsize=8, currsize=8)` and a subsequent `_clear_all_native_caches()` leaves currsize at 8 - the calibration retained 8 native PLDs it will never reuse (every probe has a distinct noise multiplier, hence hits=0). (b) Holding 8 distinct `random_allocation_gaussian_pld(sigma_i, 64, 4, default_config)` handles grew RSS from 19.5 MB to 199.7 MB (+180.3 MB, ~22 MB per entry, ~45x the documented 0.5 MB); dropping them returned RSS to 117.0 MB. A long-lived service that calibrates several k-out-of-t or balls-in-bins configurations therefore carries ~100-180 MB of Rust PLD grids the API contract says are released.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_random_allocation_cache.py:5-9 - 'The cache is a bounded LRU over immutable Python :class:`Pld` objects (no native handles), so it is self-limiting and needs no byte budget or destructor.'
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_random_allocation_cache.py:24-27 - '~0.5 MB per entry at the default config'

packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/calibration.py:356-357 - `finally: _clear_all_native_caches()`; _native_cache.py:26,40-42 iterate only the `NativeCache` weak registry, which this lru_cache never joins
measured: CacheInfo(hits=0, misses=14, maxsize=8, currsize=8) after calibrate and after _clear_all_native_caches(); +180.3 MB RSS for 8 held handles
findings.fix_sketch: Either register this cache as a `NativeCache` (like the b-min-sep one) so its bytes are budgeted and `calibrate`'s finally clears it, or drop the second cache layer entirely - `KOutOfT.pld` and `BallsInBins.pld` are already wrapped in `@pld_cache`, and the only value `epoch_pld` adds is sharing between two processes that differ solely in a field the PLD ignores. At minimum correct the docstring: the entries are native handles and measure ~22 MB each, not 0.5 MB.

findings.title: Python 3.12 is still advertised by every wheel and executed by no CI lane
findings.claim: Slate #428 ('Test the supported Python 3.12 runtime') is still unmet at 12146ec4. Every explicit interpreter version in `.github/workflows/` is 3.11 or 3.13; `validate-distributions.yml:19` matrixes exactly `["3.11", "3.13"]` and `python-tests.yml:37` defaults to 3.11. Meanwhile the root `pyproject.toml:12,29` and every package manifest declare `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"` together with the `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12` classifier, so pip resolves and installs the wheels on 3.12. I re-checked this because #428 is a Slate issue in my scope; it is also OPQ-386 / Bazalt #841, which is closed.
findings.failure_scenario: A 3.12-only regression - a dependency resolving to a different wheel on 3.12, or interpreter-specific behaviour in the torch.func / optree layer - ships in a release whose metadata explicitly advertises 3.12 support, and no CI signal has ever existed for it. Users on 3.12 are the first to see it. Bounded: 3.11 and 3.13 bracket most interpreter-sensitive behaviour, and nothing here changes a privacy guarantee.
evidence: grep over .github/workflows: ci.yml:56 '3.11', :69 '3.13', :117 '3.11', :131 '3.13'; pr.yml:96 '3.11', :109 '3.13', :165 '3.11', :182 '3.13'; validate-distributions.yml:19 python-version: ["3.11", "3.13"]; python-tests.yml:37 default: "3.11" - no occurrence of 3.12 anywhere

pyproject.toml:12 `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.14"`; pyproject.toml:29 `"Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12"`; the same classifier appears in packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml:23, packages/opaque-alignment/pyproject.toml:26, packages/opaque-auditing/pyproject.toml and the rest
findings.fix_sketch: Add one cheap 3.12 leg - the `validate-distributions` install scenario is the smallest - or drop the 3.12 classifier and narrow `requires-python` so endpoints-only testing becomes an explicit documented policy rather than the residue of the #665 version bump.

delta_reviewed: Scope: regression re-verification of the 94 closed Slate (July) issues against the 124-commit delta 4b13d82..12146ec4, prioritising the fixes most exposed to it, plus a read of the whole delta in those fix sites. Environment note: the in-tree opaque_accounting.abi3.so was stale (Aug 27, missing poisson_pld and 90 tests failed against it); I ran everything against a current-source overlay build (verified byte-identical Python sources to HEAD) via PYTHONPATH.
